title: Recovery Records as Training Data
summary: Work through Recovery Records as Training Data.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Recovery Records as Training Data**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Fine-Tuning, § Recovery Records as Training Data
blocks.md: Consider a recovery demonstration admitted by the curation pipeline for the repair agent (a later section) into `repair_demonstrations_v1`. During the recorded session, the agent generated a malformed edit proposal that the runtime validator refused prior to tool dispatch. In response to the failure notification, the model inspected the tool schema, generated a corrected edit, and produced candidate patch `ws_r20`. From this multi-turn trajectory, the target-selection policy `recovery_targets_v1` marks three assistant turns as supervised targets: the schema inspection request (`e3`), the corrected edit (`e4`), and the scoped final summary (`e6`).

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Loss masking matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Loss is placed only on selected policy-response positions while prompts, refused proposals, and observations stay as attended context with zero loss, because a trajectory has two authors and only one is trained.

questions.q: The section **Recovery Records as Training Data** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Packing is only a memory layout, so block-diagonal attention, per-example label shifts, and position handling must leave each packed example's logits equal to its unpacked logits, a property tested rather than assumed.
A training example reconstructs each selected response's input exactly as the model received it, truncations and redactions included, under a recorded tokenizer and template configuration.
LoRA cuts trainable parameters but parameter state falls only by the byte ratio of trainable to frozen state, and adapters give modularity, not isolation.

Loss is placed only on selected policy-response positions while prompts, refused proposals, and observations stay as attended context with zero loss, because a trajectory has two authors and only one is trained.

questions.explanation: This section develops **Loss masking**: Loss is placed only on selected policy-response positions while prompts, refused proposals, and observations stay as attended context with zero loss, because a trajectory has two authors and only one is trained.

questions.hint: Think about which later idea this concept feeds.
